label: At GO late in the episode, fires after a rewarded a2-to-S2 trial, growing with trial index.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * last_is('a2 S2 r') * np.maximum(ep_trial - 65, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 65, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is('?') * np.maximum(ep_trial - 65, 0)
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * (ep_dec >= 6) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 60, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 60, 0) * (prev_reward != 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 60, 0) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial-60,0) * belief_lo
explanation: Active only at GO and only late in the episode (trial >~65). The magnitude is set by an interaction of the previous trial and time: after a common a2->S2 rewarded trial it fires strongly (~1.3-2.2) with amplitude growing with ep_trial; after every other previous-trial pattern (including rare-rewarded a2->S1 and all a1 trials) it is near zero, which the second term encodes as a negative ramp that cancels the additive timing baseline. Belief (S2 good) correlates but adds little once the previous trial is known. Remaining error: window-first trials where the previous trial is unknown, and minor shape of the time ramp; the 7-term free fit (0.71 dev) mainly refines the ramp shape versus the 2-term short form (0.65 dev).

issues: The recorded short form reproduces at 0.6508 test R^2 beyond timing; changing the ramp to start at 60 gives 0.648.
The claim that magnitude grows with ep_trial holds. A step indicator, (ep_trial >= 66), in place of the ramp scores 0.515, against 0.651 for the ramp.

The claim that rare-rewarded a2->S1 is near zero holds. In the profile its GO residual is -0.123, the same as the a1 patterns and a2 S2 u. Adding a last_is('a2 S1 r') ramp term adds only 0.001 (0.652).

The claim that belief adds little once the previous trial is known holds. Adding (phase==GO)*last_is('a2 S2 r')*belief_lo gives 0.651. Belief alone in place of the previous trial, (phase==GO)*(belief_lo<0)*ramp plus the ramp, gives only 0.372.
Within a2 S2 r, the trial two back and a constant offset each add under 0.001. The ramp shape carries the amplitude.

The second term (negative ramp) is a correction against the additive timing baseline. It is still a legitimate description: the feature fires only after a2 S2 r, so the late-episode baseline has to be cancelled on every other pattern. Without it the score falls to 0.51.

Running misses leaves one systematic error class: GO on window-first trials, where the previous trial is unknown, are under-predicted by +0.092 (actual about 2.1, predicted about 0.1). All other cells are within 0.04. The explanation acknowledges this. Adding (phase == GO) * last_is('?') * ramp raises the test score to 0.724. This is a data-coverage effect (the agent did see that trial), not new mechanism.
There is a small isolated miss at ep_trial 99 (predicted 2.08, actual 0). Adding an (ep_trial == 99) term gains only 0.001.
